title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 26.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 26, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Uzziah was made king at sixteen years old
Uzziah broke down the wall of Gath
God helped Uzziah against the Philistines
Uzziah sought God in the days of Zechariah
questions.correctAnswer: Uzziah was made king at sixteen years old
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in the chapter is that Uzziah was made king at sixteen years old, as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:1.

questions.question: How old was Uzziah when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:3 states that Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: Who was Uzziah's mother?
questions.explanation: The verse 2 Chronicles 26:3 mentions that Uzziah's mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Uzziah do after the king slept with his fathers?
options: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah
He sought God in the days of Zechariah
He broke down the wall of Jabneh
questions.correctAnswer: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:2 states that Uzziah built Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.

questions.question: How long did Uzziah reign in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 26:3, Uzziah reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Uzziah do that was right in the sight of the LORD?
options: He did according to all that his father Amaziah did
He gave gifts to the Ammonites
He sought God in the days of Zechariah
questions.correctAnswer: He did according to all that his father Amaziah did
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:4 explains that Uzziah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah did.

questions.question: Who did Uzziah seek in the days of Zechariah?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:5 states that Uzziah sought God in the days of Zechariah.

questions.question: What was Zechariah known for according to the text?
options: Understanding in the visions of God
Being a warrior against the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding in the visions of God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:5 describes Zechariah as having understanding in the visions of God.

questions.question: Which walls did Uzziah break down in his wars?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:6 says Uzziah broke down the wall of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod.

questions.question: Who helped Uzziah against the Philistines and other groups?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:7 states that God helped Uzziah against the Philistines and other groups.

questions.question: Which people gave gifts to Uzziah?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:8 says the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah.

questions.question: Did Uzziah strengthen himself exceedingly?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:8 states that Uzziah strengthened himself exceedingly.

questions.question: Is it true that Uzziah's name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 26:8, Uzziah's name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt.

questions.question: Did Uzziah marry the daughter of Zechariah according to 2 Chronicles 26?
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Uzziah marrying the daughter of Zechariah in 2 Chronicles 26.

questions.question: Does 2 Chronicles 26 say Uzziah conquered Egypt?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26 does not say that Uzziah conquered Egypt; it only mentions his name spreading to the entering in of Egypt (verse 8).

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Uzziah build in Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 26:9?
questions.explanation: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, valley gate, and other locations as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:9.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 26:5 promise will happen if someone seeks the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:5 states that as long as Uzziah sought the LORD, God made him to prosper.

questions.question: How many chief of the fathers of the mighty men of valor were there according to 2 Chronicles 26:12?
questions.explanation: The whole number of the chief of the fathers of the mighty men of valor was two thousand and six hundred as recorded in 2 Chronicles 26:12.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 26:7 reveal about God's help to Uzziah?
options: God helped him against the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: God helped him against the Philistines
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:7 shows that God helped Uzziah against the Philistines and other enemies.

questions.question: What type of equipment did Uzziah prepare for his army according to 2 Chronicles 26:14?
questions.explanation: Uzziah prepared shields, spears, helmets, habergeons, bows, and slings as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:14.

questions.question: How did Uzziah's name spread abroad according to 2 Chronicles 26:15?
questions.explanation: Uzziah's name spread far because he was marvellously helped until he was strong, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 26:15.

questions.question: What does Uzziah's story warn about pride according to 2 Chronicles 26:16?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:16 indicates that Uzziah's pride led to his destruction when he transgressed against the LORD.

questions.question: How long did Uzziah reign according to 2 Chronicles 26:3?
questions.explanation: Uzziah reigned for fifty and two years in Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:3.

questions.question: What action did Uzziah take against the cities of the Philistines according to 2 Chronicles 26:6?
questions.explanation: Uzziah broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod as a military action against the Philistines as described in 2 Chronicles 26:6.

questions.question: What was Uzziah's mother's name according to 2 Chronicles 26:3?
questions.explanation: Uzziah's mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem, as noted in 2 Chronicles 26:3.

questions.question: What did Uzziah build in the desert according to 2 Chronicles 26:10?
questions.explanation: Uzziah built towers in the desert and dug many wells as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:10.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 26:11 say about Uzziah's military?
options: He had a host of fighting men
questions.correctAnswer: He had a host of fighting men
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:11 states that Uzziah had an army of fighting men that went out to war by bands.

questions.question: What is true about Uzziah's initial reign according to 2 Chronicles 26:4?
questions.explanation: Uzziah did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to 2 Chronicles 26:4.

questions.question: The Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah according to 2 Chronicles 26:8. True or False?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:8 confirms that the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah.

questions.question: Uzziah's pride led to his immediate success. True or False?
questions.explanation: Uzziah's pride ultimately led to his destruction, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 26:16.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 26.

questions.question: Who went in after Uzziah to confront him about burning incense?
questions.explanation: Azariah the priest went in after him, as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:17.

questions.question: How many priests accompanied Azariah to confront Uzziah?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions 'fourscore priests of the LORD' accompanying Azariah in 2 Chronicles 26:17.

questions.question: What did the priests tell Uzziah regarding burning incense?
questions.explanation: The priests declared it 'appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the LORD, but to the priests', as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:18.

questions.question: What happened to Uzziah when he became angry with the priests?
questions.explanation: Uzziah became wroth and was struck with leprosy in his forehead as noted in 2 Chronicles 26:19.

questions.question: What was Uzziah's condition until the day of his death?
questions.explanation: Uzziah was a leper until his death, as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:21.

questions.question: Who wrote about the acts of Uzziah?
questions.explanation: Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz, wrote the acts of Uzziah, as noted in 2 Chronicles 26:22.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'priest' in 2 Chronicles 26:18 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'priest' (kohen) suggests a mediator between God and the people, as they performed sacred duties.

questions.question: What literary device is used when the priests confront Uzziah in a united front?
questions.explanation: The priests' confrontation of Uzziah exemplifies parallelism through their unified declaration against his actions.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Uzziah's arrogance in 2 Chronicles 26:16?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:18 states, 'Pride goes before destruction,' connecting to Uzziah's downfall due to his arrogance.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects on the consequences of pride similar to Uzziah's in 2 Chronicles 26:16?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:12 states, 'Whoever exalts himself will be humbled,' mirroring Uzziah's pride and subsequent judgment.

questions.question: What precedes the event of Uzziah burning incense in the temple in 2 Chronicles 26:18?
questions.explanation: Uzziah's pride led him to transgress against the LORD by attempting to burn incense, as highlighted in 2 Chronicles 26:16.

questions.question: What does Uzziah's leprosy symbolize in the context of his reign in 2 Chronicles 26:21?
questions.explanation: Uzziah's leprosy symbolizes God's judgment for his act of pride and disobedience, as seen in 2 Chronicles 26:21.

questions.question: Uzziah's actions led to him being cut off from which place according to 2 Chronicles 26:21?
questions.explanation: Uzziah was cut off from the house of the LORD due to his leprosy, as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:21.

questions.question: True or False: Uzziah died a respected king without any consequences for his actions.
questions.explanation: Uzziah faced severe consequences for his actions, living as a leper until his death, as noted in 2 Chronicles 26:21.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah the prophet documented the acts of Uzziah.
questions.explanation: Isaiah the prophet documented the acts of Uzziah, as stated in 2 Chronicles 26:22.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 26:5 teach about God's providence and human prosperity?
options: God blesses and prospers those who diligently seek Him through faithful spiritual counsel
Human prosperity is solely the result of personal effort and military success
Prosperity is random and unrelated to one's relationship with God
Seeking God has no impact on earthly success
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses and prospers those who diligently seek Him through faithful spiritual counsel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:5 states that as long as Uzziah sought the LORD through Zechariah who had understanding in the visions of God, God made him prosper, illustrating God's providential blessing on faithful seeking.

questions.question: What doctrine about human pride and judgment does 2 Chronicles 26:16 teach?
options: Human pride leads to destruction and divine judgment
Pride is a virtue that leads to divine favor
God ignores human arrogance when the person is powerful
Human sin can be overlooked if one has military success
questions.correctAnswer: Human pride leads to destruction and divine judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:16 shows that when Uzziah became strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction because he transgressed against God, demonstrating the biblical doctrine that pride leads to judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the priesthood and worship does 2 Chronicles 26:18 teach?
options: Only the consecrated sons of Aaron have authority to perform priestly duties like burning incense
Any king can perform all religious rites without restriction
Worship practices are flexible and not bound by divine law
The priesthood can be replaced by royal authority
questions.correctAnswer: Only the consecrated sons of Aaron have authority to perform priestly duties like burning incense
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:18 emphasizes the exclusive priestly role of Aaron's descendants in burning incense, highlighting the doctrine of divinely instituted priesthood and worship order.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 26:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:7 states that God helped Uzziah against various enemies, demonstrating God's sovereign power over nations and battles.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 26:20 illustrate in God's treatment of Uzziah?
questions.explanation: Verse 20 shows that God smote Uzziah with leprosy for entering the sanctuary unlawfully, reflecting God's holiness and intolerance of sin in His presence.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 26:1-3 prepare the theme of divine blessing and subsequent judgment in the monarchy as seen in later biblical narratives?
options: It introduces the pattern of a king's initial faithfulness followed by pride and downfall
It depicts a perfect king who never fails God
It emphasizes that age determines the quality of kingship
It shows that dynastic succession guarantees God's approval
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces the pattern of a king's initial faithfulness followed by pride and downfall
questions.explanation: These verses present Uzziah's early reign marked by faithfulness, setting up the narrative arc of blessing and judgment common in Israel's monarchy.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Chronicles 26:22-23 connect prophetical writing to royal history and judgment?
options: It shows that prophets like Isaiah recorded kings' acts, linking divine revelation with historical events
It denies the involvement of prophets in royal affairs
It presents royal history as independent from prophetic insight
It implies prophets only recorded positive deeds
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that prophets like Isaiah recorded kings' acts, linking divine revelation with historical events
questions.explanation: Verse 22 notes Isaiah wrote about Uzziah, demonstrating the prophetic role in documenting and interpreting kings' reigns, integrating theology with history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 16 and 20 teach about sin and divine judgment?
options: Prideful sin leads to immediate and tangible divine punishment
God is slow to punish sin and often overlooks it
Sin has no real consequences in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Prideful sin leads to immediate and tangible divine punishment
questions.explanation: Verse 16 describes Uzziah's prideful trespass, and verse 20 describes his immediate affliction with leprosy as judgment, showing the direct consequences of sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 5 and 15 teach about divine assistance in human endeavors?
options: God prospers and marvelously helps those who seek Him, enabling success in both spiritual and military efforts
Human success is independent of divine help
Divine help is only for spiritual matters, not for military strength
God's help is unpredictable and unrelated to human faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God prospers and marvelously helps those who seek Him, enabling success in both spiritual and military efforts
questions.explanation: Verse 5 notes God prospered Uzziah as he sought the LORD, and verse 15 describes God's marvelous help in military inventions and strength, linking divine blessing to comprehensive success.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 18 and 21 teach about sanctification and separation from God’s presence due to sin?
options: Sin leads to exclusion from sacred fellowship and separation from the house of the LORD
Sin does not affect one’s access to God’s sanctuary
Leprosy symbolized divine favor and inclusion
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to exclusion from sacred fellowship and separation from the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 18 forbids Uzziah's unauthorized priestly act, and verse 21 shows his leprosy caused him to dwell separately, illustrating the doctrine of sanctification requiring separation from sin.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the punishment of Uzziah with leprosy was an unfair and harsh response to a king’s zeal for worship. What does 2 Chronicles 26:16-20 actually teach?
options: God’s holiness requires strict boundaries in worship; Uzziah transgressed these, resulting in just judgment
God arbitrarily punishes those who enter the temple
Kings are above religious law and should not be punished
Leprosy was a natural disease unrelated to sin
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness requires strict boundaries in worship; Uzziah transgressed these, resulting in just judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 16-20 demonstrate that Uzziah's pride led him to unlawfully burn incense, violating God's holiness and priestly laws, which brought a divinely ordained punishment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of divine blessing is illustrated by 2 Chronicles 26:9-10?
options: God’s blessing includes provision for both military defense and agricultural prosperity
Divine blessing is limited to spiritual matters only
Material success is unrelated to God’s favor
God blesses only through miraculous means
questions.correctAnswer: God’s blessing includes provision for both military defense and agricultural prosperity
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 describe Uzziah building defensive towers and digging wells for his cattle and crops, showing that God’s blessing encompasses comprehensive national wellbeing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 2 Chronicles 26:8 concerning Uzziah's renown and strength?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states Uzziah’s name spread to Egypt because he strengthened himself exceedingly, which the text attributes to God’s help, reflecting God’s omnipotent power enabling earthly strength.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 26:11-13 contribute to the biblical understanding of divine order in military organization?
options: God ordains structured leadership and accountability in the use of military force for His purposes
Military power is chaotic and unstructured in biblical history
Victory comes without any human leadership or planning
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains structured leadership and accountability in the use of military force for His purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 describe Uzziah’s army organized by captains and scribes, showing divinely sanctioned order in warfare aligned with God’s providential guidance.

questions.question: What narrative arc does 2 Chronicles 26:19-21 fulfill in the broader biblical theme of sin and exile?
options: It exemplifies how sin results in separation and exile even for kings, prefiguring Israel’s national exile
It shows that sin has no consequences for rulers
It denies any connection between sin and physical affliction
It suggests that exile is unrelated to disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies how sin results in separation and exile even for kings, prefiguring Israel’s national exile
questions.explanation: Uzziah’s leprosy and isolation in verses 19-21 symbolize how sin leads to separation from God’s presence and community, foreshadowing Israel’s exile.
